title: session-circuit-adapter: unify session/stream ergonomics, auth retries, and parity fixes across SDKs
author: Priya Menon
body:
Summary: This PR introduces the SessionCircuit adapter — a thin, cross-language surface that unifies credential windowing, retry presets, and a lightweight circuit-style session for streaming connectors. The goal is to: 1) provide a single mental model for credential refresh and short-lived leases across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs; 2) normalize retry profiles with clearer presets for interactive vs. batch streaming; 3) remove several SDK-specific shims so that session/stream ergonomics are consistent across languages; and 4) bump SDK package versions to reflect the compatibility contract.

Motivation and context: Over the past year we've accumulated multiple, slightly-different session/credential patterns across the three SDKs. That has led to mapping bugs in internal services (SUP-5312) and made polyglot clients harder to reason about. The SessionCircuit adapter provides a common behavioral contract: short-lived Lease tokens (TTL window), a circuit state (healthy/hesitant/tripped) to guide backoff decisions, and a minimal pull-stream facade for consumers. This is intentionally small: adapters are pluggable and backward-compatible; existing constructor helpers are deprecated with clear migration notes.

What changed (high-level):
- Core contract: added SessionCircuit interface (conceptual) implemented as SessionCircuitPy, SessionCircuitTS, SessionCircuitGo in the respective SDKs. These share the same lifecycle events: acquire/renew/release + onCircuitChange hooks.
- Auth + retries: standardized retry profiles (interactive, streaming, batch) and wired them into session lifecycle backoffs. Introduced a default hedged retry window for short-lived credentials to avoid thundering renewals.
- Streaming ergonomics: exposed a small PullStream facade (next, cancel, onClose) and an EventEmitter/async-iterator adapter for TS/Py to match pro-consumer patterns. Go exposes a Channel-iterator idiom.
- Parity fixes: aligned typed error enums (ErrAuthExpired / ErrSessionTripped) and common status codes across SDKs to make behavior deterministic for routing/fallback in the runtime.
- Deprecations: removed legacy session shims (SessionV1) and added Migration guide snippets in SDK docs.
- Version bumps: python 0.9.0 -> 0.9.1, typescript 1.7.0 -> 1.8.0, go v1.6.0 -> v1.7.0.

Commits (summary):
- 7c33a2f: introduce session-circuit core interfaces and tests (cross-lang spec).
- 9b2f0a1: python: SessionCircuit implementation + async iterator adapter + docs.
- 4d8b9ea: typescript: EventedStream + session lease manager + ergonomic factory.
- e52f74b: go: CircuitSessionFactory + channel iterator + typed errors.
- 0a1c4f7: common: retry preset registry, tests, CI matrix updates.
- 6f7de3b: docs: migration guide + examples + release notes.

Files changed (high level examples):
- sdk/python/redwood/session_circuit.py (new), sdk/python/streaming_async.py (adapter), sdk/python/tests/test_session_circuit.py
- sdk/typescript/src/session/circuit.ts (new), sdk/typescript/src/stream/pullstream.ts (adapter), sdk/typescript/tests/session.spec.ts
- sdk/go/session/circuit.go (new), sdk/go/stream/pulliter.go, sdk/go/errors/errs.go
- docs/sdk/migrations/session-circuit.md, docs/sdk/examples/session-circuit-quickstart.md
- ci/tooling/matrix.yml (add py/ts/go matrix for session tests)

Small illustrative snippet (python adapter usage):
from redwood import SessionCircuit
with SessionCircuit(cred_provider, retry_preset='interactive') as session:
    stream = session.open_pullstream(model='rwr/small')
    for chunk in stream:
        process(chunk)

Review notes and design decisions:
- Circuit states: healthy/hesitant/tripped — this model maps to runtime routing (fast path vs. conservative path). We debated explicit token prefetch vs. on-demand renew; settled on conservative prefetch with jitter to reduce correlated renewals.
- Backoff presets: interactive uses short jittered backoff (50-200ms), streaming uses a medium window with bounded retries, batch uses exponential floor/backoff. Presets are configurable by advanced users.
- Compatibility: the adapter implements a backwards-compatible facade: existing helper constructors still work but now log a one-line deprecation warning directing users to the new factory.

CI and testing: initial CI run failed on lint (import order) and a flaky go test that relied on time-based sleeps. I pushed two followups: fix import order and replace time.Sleep with a testable clock interface. CI rerun: all checks green (unit, integration, linters, contract-tests). Full CI summary: build (pass), unit tests (pass), integration session matrix (pass), linters (pass).

Review conversation (high level):
- Evan Park (reviewer): "Nice consolidation. Please tighten the doc examples to show migration path from SessionV1 and call out any behavioral differences for token refresh windows."
- Author (Priya): "Added migration guide and a small FAQ section. Clarified that the default window is slightly larger than the legacy V1 to reduce renew storms. Tests added to demonstrate backward-compatible behavior."
- Rosa Alvarez: "TS ergonomics look good but ensure the EventedStream doesn't leak listeners on cancel."
- Author: "Added unit tests to assert listener cleanup and a small lifecycle hook; also removed a lingering setTimeout in the adapter."
- Jonah Fischer: "Go iterator design is idiomatic but please ensure error types are annotated for easy mapping in the runtime router."
- Author: "Aligned error enums across SDKs and added mapping table in docs. Also added a couple of integration tests to exercise an end-to-end fallback scenario."

Approvals: Evan (approved), Rosa (approved after changes), Jonah (approved).

Release notes (short):
- Introduce SessionCircuit adapter: unified session/credential surface across SDKs. (non-breaking; migration guide provided)
- New retry presets: interactive/streaming/batch.
- Streaming ergonomic improvements: PullStream adapters and EventedStream for TS; async iterator parity in Py; channel iterators in Go.
- Version bumps: python -> 0.9.1, typescript -> 1.8.0, go -> v1.7.0.

Migration guidance (short):
- Most users can swap SessionV1(...) with SessionCircuit.factory(...) and opt-in to the retry_preset that matches prior behavior. See docs/sdk/migrations/session-circuit.md for examples.

Follow-ups and TODOs (tracked in ENG-1987):
- Add telemetry to measure renew jitter effectiveness in production (instrument events for renew attempts).
- Consider a global session pool for high-throughput multi-tenant hosts (design spike).
- Add more end-to-end scenario tests in perf-canary for long-running streams.

Merge outcome: after approvals and green CI the branch was squashed and merged into main on 2026-02-25. Tags and SDK package releases were staged by release tooling; package publishing jobs are scheduled to run as part of the next release window.

Notes: This PR purposefully keeps the public surface minimal and well-documented. If you want to prototype an aggressive prefetch or alternate circuit semantics, implement a custom SessionCircuitProvider and register it through the factory.
